collected_dynamic_variables.call_volume: about 10 calls a week missed; ~40% could book
collected_dynamic_variables.pain_points: answering service misses calls,answering service doesn’t convert inquiries into bookings effectively,needs signed BAA/HIPAA assurances, wants dental references

transcript:
User: Hi. Saw your ad. Honestly I doubt this is for us but go ahead.
Agent: Got it — thanks for being upfront. What about the ad made you pause and click in the first place?
User: I’m curious, but we already have an answering service. Why should I consider changing?
Agent: Yeah, makes sense — if you’re already paying for coverage, switching only matters if you’re still losing calls or getting a clunky customer experience. What’s the one thing your answering service does today that bugs you most?
User: They sometimes miss calls or don't manage to convert inquiries into bookings effectively. That's a problem for us.
Agent: Yeah, that’s frustrating — it kind of defeats the point of paying for an answering service. Roughly how many calls a week do you think are getting missed or not turning into bookings?
User: We miss about 10 calls a week, and I’d say 40% of those would potentially book appointments.
Agent: Got it — so that’s roughly 4 potential bookings a week slipping through. What kind of business is this for (what industry)?
User: This is for my dental practice in Phoenix, Arizona. We don't do daylight saving here. What's this going to cost?
Agent: Got it — Phoenix, and no DST helps. Before I quote anything, is your main goal to capture more new-patient appointment calls during treatment hours, after-hours emergencies, or both?
User: Both are important, but capturing new-patient appointment calls during treatment hours is my main priority.
Agent: Makes sense — that’s exactly when your front desk is tied up. Mind if I do a super quick 30‑second calculation on what those missed calls are costing you?
User: Sure, go ahead, but make it quick. I’m still waiting on a cost estimate from you.
Agent: Totally — I’ll be quick, and I’ll get back to cost right after this. What’s your average value of a new-patient appointment for you in dollars?
User: $700 on average. Now, what’s this going to cost? Give me a number now or I'm done.
Agent: I hear you. Based on your numbers, if you book 40% of those 10 missed calls at $700, that’s about $2800 a week—about $12100/mo—does that sound right?

On cost: it depends on your call volume and what you want it to handle (new-patient booking plus after-hours emergencies), so Jay covers exact pricing on the live call—if it’s in the ballpark, are you open to a quick walkthrough?
User: I need a ballpark now. What do comparable services cost, roughly?
Agent: Got it — ballpark, most practices see it land around **$1,200 to $2,800 per month**, depending on call volume and what you want handled (new-patient booking + after-hours emergencies). Is that in the range you were expecting?
User: Alright, that range is what I expected. But how do I know you're not a sketchy startup disappearing with data?
Agent: Totally fair to ask. What would you need to see to feel comfortable—things like a signed BAAs/HIPAA approach, where call recordings are stored, or a short list of current dental references?
User: I’d need to see signed BAAs and references from dental practices like mine to feel comfortable.
Agent: Got it — we can share a signed BAA/HIPAA approach and dental references as part of the walkthrough with Jay. It’s a 20-minute walkthrough this week… what’s better for you—later today or tomorrow?
User: Tomorrow afternoon works for me. But last year, I tried AI and it wasted three months. Why is this different?
Agent: Oof—yeah, I hear you; a bad AI rollout can burn a lot of time. What specifically went wrong last time (couldn’t book correctly, sounded robotic, integration issues, or something else)?
User: It couldn't book correctly and sounded too robotic. Patients were frustrated, and it didn't integrate well with our systems.
Agent: Got it — if it couldn’t reliably book and it sounded robotic, patients will bail fast. When you say “integrate,” what system was it supposed to book into—Dentrix, Eaglesoft, Open Dental, or something else?
User: We're using Dentrix. If this works better, I’ll book a live call tomorrow afternoon.
Agent: Got it — Dentrix. What’s your first name?
User: It’s Brenda. So, are we set for the live call tomorrow afternoon? Want to be sure.
Agent: Got it, Brenda — not quite set yet; I still need your last name to get it booked. What’s your last name?
User: Kowalski. Book the call for tomorrow afternoon, please. Confirm it's set.
Agent: Got it, Brenda Kowalski — what’s the name of your dental practice?
User: Desert Bloom Dental in Phoenix. Confirm we're on for tomorrow afternoon's call, please. I want to be sure.
Agent: Got it — Desert Bloom Dental. Before I can lock a time in, is the number you’re calling from the best contact number to reach you?
User: Actually, use +16025550017. Confirm the call is set for tomorrow afternoon, please.
Agent: Got it — I’ll use that number. Quick check: you’re on **Mountain time**, right?
User: We go by Arizona time — it's the same as Mountain, but no daylight saving here. Confirm the call, please.
Agent: You’re right — Arizona time. For tomorrow afternoon, I can do **1:30 PM** or **3:00 PM** Arizona time; which works?
User: Let's do 3:00 PM Arizona time. Thanks for your patience and see you tomorrow.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: My calendar is giving me trouble right now, but I’m going to try that again.
Agent: My calendar is giving me trouble right now. We’re having trouble confirming the calendar — we’ll reach you at your number within the hour to lock in **3:00 PM Arizona time**.
User: Sure, I'll wait. Just need to ensure everything’s good for tomorrow.
Agent: I hear you, Brenda. I’m not able to confirm it on my side right this second—can you do **2:15 PM Arizona time** tomorrow instead?
User: 2:15 PM Arizona time works. Let's confirm everything for then. Thanks!
Agent: One moment while I lock in 2:15 PM Arizona time for tomorrow.
Agent: My calendar is giving me trouble right now — it’s not accepting the phone number format on my side. Can you confirm the best callback number again, including the country code (for example, +1…)?
User: Perfect. I'll be ready at 2:15 PM Arizona time. Looking forward to it. Thank you.
Agent: Got it — I’m still not able to fully confirm it on my side until the phone number validates. What’s the best callback number again in full, including country code (like +1…)?
User: Use +16025550017. That’s the correct number with country code. Confirm the call once it's validated.
Agent: Got it — +16025550017. My calendar is giving me trouble right now, so I can’t validate it on my side, but the live call is intended for **tomorrow at 2:15 PM Arizona time** for Desert Bloom Dental. Are you available 5 minutes before in case Jay calls a touch early?
User: Yes, I'll be available 5 minutes early. Looking forward to it. Thanks for accommodating.
Agent: Perfect — thanks, Brenda. We’ll plan for tomorrow at 2:15 PM Arizona time, and being available a few minutes early is great. Have a good rest of your day.
